function.description: This function is used to create a recommendation model using a given user data and an algorithm type Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

user_data.description: A data frame of user ratings. Rows represent users, columns represent items, and entries represent user ratings for items

algorithm.description: The algorithm to be used for creating the recommendation model. Collaborative filtering, content-based filtering and hybrid filtering.

matrix_factorization.description: Optional parameter to indicate whether matrix factorization should be used. Default is False.

Below is a practical, step‑by‑step guide you can follow to build a modern, high‑performance frontend for your e‑commerce site. I’ll cover the whole pipeline—from choosing a tech stack to deploying the finished product—so you can pick the parts that fit your team’s skill set and your business goals. --- ## 1️⃣ Define Your Requirements & Constraints | What | Why it matters | |------|----------------| | **Target devices** (desktop, mobile, tablet) | Determines responsive strategy | | **Core features** (product catalog, cart, checkout, search, reviews, admin panel) | Drives component architecture | | **Performance goals** (first paint < 2 s, interactive < 5 s) | Influences bundling, lazy loading | | **SEO needs** (indexable product pages, rich snippets) | Requires server‑side rendering or prerendering | | **Accessibility** (WCAG 2.1 AA) | Improves usability & compliance | | **Team expertise** (React, Vue, Angular, Svelte, etc.) | Affects learning curve & productivity | | **Budget & timeline** | Guides tool selection (open source vs paid services) | > **Tip:** Create a “feature backlog” and rank items by business value. That will keep the scope manageable. --- ## 2️⃣ Pick a Frontend Stack | Option | Pros | Cons | Typical Use‑Case | |--------|------|------|------------------| | **React + Vite / CRA** | Huge ecosystem, flexible, great community | Boilerplate can grow | Most e‑commerce sites | | **Vue 3 + Vite** | Simpler learning curve, composable API | Smaller ecosystem than React | Startups, MVPs | | **Angular** | Opinionated, built‑in DI, CLI | Steeper learning curve | Enterprise apps | | **SvelteKit** | Zero runtime overhead, fast builds | Smaller ecosystem | Performance‑critical sites | | **Next.js (React)** | SSR + SSG, file‑based routing, image optimization | Slightly heavier | SEO‑heavy product pages | | **Nuxt.js (Vue)** | Similar to Next.js but for Vue | Same trade‑offs | SEO‑heavy sites with Vue | ### Recommendation If you’re starting fresh and want a balance between flexibility and performance, **React + Vite** (or **Next.js** if SEO is critical) is a solid choice. If you already have a Vue background, **Nuxt.js** gives you the same benefits as Next.js. --- ## 3️⃣ Set Up Project Skeleton ```bash # Example with Vite + React npm create vite@latest ecommerce-frontend --template react cd ecommerce-frontend npm install ``` Add essential libraries: ```bash # State management npm i @tanstack/react-query # For async data fetching npm i zustand # Or Redux Toolkit if you prefer # Routing npm i react-router-dom # Styling npm i tailwindcss postcss autoprefixer npx tailwindcss init -p # Icons npm i lucide-react # Testing npm i jest @testing-library/react @testing-library/jest-dom # Linting & Formatting npm i eslint prettier eslint-plugin-react eslint-config-prettier eslint-plugin-prettier ``` Configure Tailwind in `tailwind.config.js` and import it in `src/index.css`. --- ## 4️⃣ Design the Component Architecture | Layer | Responsibility | Suggested Libraries | |-------|----------------|---------------------| | **UI Components** | Reusable visual elements (buttons, cards, modals) | `@headlessui/react`, `react-icons` | | **Feature Pages** | Page‑specific logic (Home, ProductDetail, Cart) | React Router + React Query | | **State Store** | Global state (cart, auth, filters) | Zustand or Redux Toolkit | | **API Client** | HTTP requests, caching, optimistic updates | Axios + React Query | | **Utilities** | Helpers (formatting, validation) | `date-fns`, `yup` | | **Testing** | Unit & integration tests | Jest + RTL | > **Folder Structure Example** ``` src/ ├─ api/ │ └─ client.ts # Axios instance + interceptors ├─ components/ │ ├─ ui/ # Button, Input, Modal │ └─ layout/ # Header, Footer, Sidebar ├─ features/ │ ├─ home/ │ │ ├─ HomePage.tsx │ │ └─ useHomeQuery.ts │ ├─ product/ │ │ ├─ ProductDetail.tsx │ │ └─ useProductQuery.ts │ └─ cart/ │ ├─ CartPage.tsx │ └─ useCartStore.ts ├─ hooks/ │ └─ useAuth.ts ├─ routes/ │ └─ AppRouter.tsx ├─ store/ │ └─ index.ts └─ utils/ └─ formatters.ts ``` --- ##
